questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.**

By the way, will you taught me how to speak in English?
questions.solution:
The erroneous segment is "**Will you taught me**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The future** is the tense used to express future events. We use the **future simple structure** to introduce** predictions**,** beliefs**, or **intentions about the future.**
 
• 
 
 When we use the **future simple tense** in its** interrogative form,** we start with **will** followed by the subject and the verb in its base form**(V1form**) and the sentence ends with a question mark?

 
 
• 
 
**Example:***** **Will you work on important projects next month?*

 
 
 
 
• 
 
*​ *So, as per the given **example **and the correct structure for** future simple tense** in its interrogative form "**Will you teach me how to speak in English**" will be there instead of "Will you taught me how to speak in English"

 
 
• 
 
 Hence, the correct answer is **option 2.**

 

**Correct Sentence: *By the way, will you teach me how to speak in English.***

• ***Example**: I listened. I **could** hear something. - implies that I was able to hear something.*
 
 
 
• In the above example sentence, could is used as the past tense of **'can'** and V1(form) of hear is used after could as per the correct grammatical context.
 
• Therefore, the most appropriate word to fill in the blank is** "hear."**
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **option 2.**

 

**Correct Passage: ** *The radio was already on. The radio **comes on **automatically at 7 o'clock to wake me **up**. I looked at the clock.** It **was already ten past seven. I had to get up quickly. I went into the shower, and I could** hear** the news on the radio. I couldn't hear it very well, but there was a story on the news about an elephant that had (5) ________ from a local circus.*

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** "Escaped".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence ***"I couldn't hear it very well, but there was a story on the news about an elephant that had (5) ________ from a local circus."*** is saying that **he heard a news story on the radio, where he got the news about an elephant that had escaped from a local circus.**
 
• The word **'escaped' **means having broken free from confinement.
 
 
• **Example: ***The bird **escaped** from the cage.*
 
 
 
• ​​​With the given meaning and example we can say that the most appropriate word to fill in the blank is** "Escaped".**
 
• The correct answer is **option 2.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__** Let's understand the meaning of the other given options :

 
• **Captured : **to take someone as a prisoner, or to take something into your possession, especially by force.(किसी को कैदी के रूप में लेना, या किसी चीज को अपने कब्जे में लेना, विशेष रूप से बल द्वारा।)
 
• **Absconded: **to go away suddenly and secretly in order to escape from somewhere. (फरार)
 
• **Released: **to give freedom or free movement to someone or something. (किसी को या किसी चीज़ को आज़ादी या आज़ादी देना)

 

**Correct Passage*****: **The radio was already on. The radio comes **on **automatically at 7 o'clock to wake me **up.** I looked at the clock.** It **was already ten past seven. I had to get up quickly. I went into the shower, and I could **hear **the news on the radio. I couldn't hear it very well, but there was a story on the news about an elephant that had** escaped **from a local circus.*
